results.title: From reactive relief to zero-casualty resolve: How Naya Bharat built a world-class disaster shield since 2014
results.description: Since 2014, under the decisive leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Bharat has transformed its disaster management from a slow, reactive relief model into a proactive, zero-casualty mission. By tripling disaster response funds to around Rs2 lakh crore, launching dedicated mitigation funds, and empowering grassroots ‘Aapada Mitra’ volunteers alongside advanced weather forecasting, the government has built a self-reliant and resilient Naya Bharat. Through landmark initiatives like the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and swift global rescue missions such as Operation Dost, Bharat has not only secured its own citizens against natural calamities but has also emerged as a trusted Vishwaguru and global leader in humanitarian assistance. On October 28, 2026, when Cyclone Arnab made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast, Bharat’s strengthened disaster management framework effectively protected lives and property. According to official assessments of the response, accurate early weather forecasting, proactive mass evacuations, seamless coordination across government agencies, and the swift deployment of NDRF and SDRF personnel kept casualties and infrastructure damage to a minimum. The operation highlighted the country’s modern, self-reliant approach to handling severe natural calamities and safeguarding its citizens. This report highlights how Bharat has modernised its disaster management system since 2014 through policy reforms, resilient infrastructure, advanced technology, increased funding, and faster emergency responses to protect lives and property. Proactive Policy Approach: Bharat moved away from reactive relief toward advance preparedness through the 2016 National Disaster Management Plan (aligned with the UN Sendai Framework) and the Prime Minister’s Ten-Point Agenda. Grassroots Volunteer Network: The Aapda Mitra scheme grew from 5,186 volunteers in 30 districts to a target of 1 lakh trained and insured community responders across 350 multi-hazard districts, alongside the Yuva Aapda Mitra initiative engaging NCC, NSS, and Bharat Scouts and Guides. Resilient Infrastructure: Bharat built cyclone shelters, evacuation roads, bridges, underground power cables, river embankments, Himalayan slope stabilization, and rockfall barriers to withstand severe weather events. Advanced Early-Warning Systems: Upgrades in weather tracking using Doppler radars, tsunami monitoring, storm-surge modelling, satellite drought assessments, and the Damini lightning-alert app, supported by the Rs 2,000 crore Mission Mausam for AI-based forecasting. Increased Funding and Rapid Action: For the 2021–26 period, allocations of Rs1.60 lakh crore for SDRF and SDMF, Rs54,770 crore for NDRF, and Rs13,693 crore for NDMF, while Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) deployment times dropped from 96 days to 8 days by 2025. Transforming Bharat’s Disaster Governance: A Shift Toward Proactive Resilience Since 2014, Bharat has fundamentally transformed its disaster governance framework, moving away from a reactive, post-disaster relief model toward a decisive, proactive strategy centred on early warnings, risk reduction, and minimising the loss of lives and property. Overcoming Past Fragmentation: Prior to 2014, despite the enactment of the Disaster Management Act of 2005, Bharat’s disaster response remained largely fragmented and reactive. Authorities often struggled with poor co-ordination, staffing shortages, and the lack of a unified operational strategy, which led to delayed responses during major crises. The Landmark National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP): A decisive turning point occurred in May 2016 with the launch of Bharat’s first comprehensive National Disaster Management Plan. Later updated in November 2019 to address climate change and localised risks, the NDMP established a clear, unified roadmap for the entire nation. Global Standards and “Build Back Better”: The NDMP aligned Bharat’s strategy with the four core priorities of the United Nations Sendai Framework (2015–2030): understanding disaster risks, strengthening governance, investing in resilience, and enhancing response preparedness. It also embedded the principle of “Build Back Better” into recovery and reconstruction efforts. The Prime Minister’s Ten-Point Agenda: Announced at the Asian Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in New Delhi in November 2016, the Prime Minister’s Ten-Point Agenda turned these broad goals into concrete action. Inclusive and Technology-Driven Development: This agenda mandated that all development sectors integrate disaster risk management into their projects. It placed a strong emphasis on safeguarding vulnerable households and small businesses, empowering women to take leadership roles in disaster management, and investing heavily in multi-hazard mapping, modern technology, and stronger institutions. Empowering Citizens on the Frontlines: Building a Self-Reliant Disaster Response Under the Modi government’s vision of Jan Bhagidari (people’s participation), Bharat has transformed disaster response from a purely government-led effort into a nationwide grassroots movement. By training ordinary citizens and youth as first responders, the nation is building a resilient, self-reliant society capable of protecting communities before formal relief forces even arrive. Massive Expansion of Aapda Mitra: Spearheaded by the Central Government through the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), the Aapda Mitra scheme trains local residents to act as immediate first responders. After a successful pilot between 2016 and 2018 that trained 5,186 volunteers across 30 flood-prone districts, the initiative was scaled up nationwide to certify and equip 1,00,000 community volunteers across 350 multi-hazard districts in every state and Union Territory. Hands-On Training by Elite Forces: Volunteers undergo an intensive five-day training program led by master trainers from the NDRF and SDRF. They learn life-saving skills including CPR, first aid, flood rescue, basic search and rescue, navigating collapsed structures, and safely evacuating vulnerable citizens. Comprehensive Gear and Insurance Protection: To ensure these grassroots heroes are well-protected, every trained volunteer receives an Emergency Responder Kit equipped with a safety helmet, life jacket, protective gear, LED torch, first-aid supplies, multi-tool knife, and emergency whistle. Additionally, the government provides each enrolled volunteer with three years of life and disability insurance coverage. Proven Impact on the Ground: Aapda Mitra volunteers have already proven their worth during major crises, including Cyclone Fani in Odisha, the Kerala floods, and the Wayanad landslide. Working shoulder-to-shoulder with local authorities, they played a crucial role in delivering early warnings, guiding evacuations, administering first aid, and distributing essential relief materials. Mobilising Bharat’s Youth with Yuva Aapda Mitra: Recognising the energy and discipline of Bharat’s youth, the government launched the Yuva Aapda Mitra initiative. This programme partners with premier youth organisations-the NCC, NSS, and Bharat Scouts and Guides-to build a dedicated cadre of young, disaster-ready citizens across the country.
